sentences.text: Draconyx was a small bipedal herbivore that roamed Portugal during the Late Jurassic period.
Researchers Gregory S. Paul estimated this animal measured 3.5 meters in length and weighed 150 kilograms.
The fossil was discovered in 1991 at Vale de Frades within the Lourinhã Formation by Carlos Anunciação.
The holotype specimen ML 357 is a partial skeleton lacking the skull, consisting of various limb bones, vertebrae, and teeth.
The species name loureiroi honors João de Loureiro, a Portuguese Jesuit priest and pioneer in Portuguese paleontology.
Histological analysis indicates the holotype specimen reached skeletal maturity between 27 and 31 years of age.
Mateus and Antunes classified Draconyx as a member of Iguanodontia and specifically Camptosauridae based on features of the teeth and femur.
Draconyx lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
A 2022 article places Draconyx within the clade Styracosterna, differing from earlier classifications.
